fact_rationales.F12: Focal enhancement along the enlarged right optic nerve is more typical of optic nerve glioma and optic nerve sheath meningioma than lymphoma.
fact_rationales.F13: Diffuse enlargement of the orbital portion of the right optic nerve and enhancement of the nerve sheath are more characteristic of optic nerve sheath meningioma.
fact_rationales.F17: The presence of an astrocytic neoplasm in the vitreous biopsy is highly suggestive of optic nerve glioma.
fact_rationales.F18: The immunohistochemical profile, including positivity for glial fibrillary acid protein and mutant IDH-1 protein, supports the diagnosis of optic nerve glioma.

fact_rationales.F16: Lack of perfusion of retinal vasculature is consistent with ischemic events, which can occur in glioblastoma and astrocytoma due to their infiltrative nature.
fact_rationales.F17: The presence of an astrocytic neoplasm in the vitreous biopsy strongly supports the diagnosis of astrocytoma, and also supports glioblastoma to a lesser extent.
fact_rationales.F18: Immunohistochemistry results showing positivity for glial fibrillary acid protein and mutant IDH-1 protein are more typical of astrocytoma and glioblastoma, and less typical of oligodendroglioma and optic neuritis.
fact_rationales.F8: Vision loss and optic disc swelling are more typical of infiltrative optic neuropathies like glioblastoma and astrocytoma.
